question: Can average input-loss curvature from a single intentionally overfit network serve as a scalable per-example memorization and dataset-audit score?

key_findings.claim: The proposed score estimates the squared input-Hessian trace without explicitly forming a Hessian.
key_findings.evidence: Rademacher-vector Hutchinson estimates plus finite gradient differences approximate Tr(H^2), and scores are averaged across training epochs to capture transient high curvature before cross-entropy margin saturation lowers it.

key_findings.claim: Curvature agrees substantially with expensive leave-subset-out memorization scores while requiring one training run.
key_findings.evidence: Cosine similarity with Feldman-Zhang scores is 0.82 on CIFAR100 and 0.72 on ImageNet with weight decay, rising to 0.90 and 0.87 on high-memorization subsets; the comparator required thousands of models.

key_findings.claim: High-curvature audits expose conflicting labels and synthetic corruption, including duplicate images missed by the comparator.
key_findings.evidence: Thirty-six of the top 60 CIFAR100 and 45 of the top 100 ImageNet examples are duplicate pairs with different labels; corruption detection AUROC ranges from at least 84.3% on CIFAR100 to roughly 93-100% on MNIST/CIFAR10 settings.

method.core_idea: Rank examples by the epoch-averaged squared curvature of cross-entropy loss with respect to input pixels.
method.mechanism: A finite-difference Hessian-vector product for random Rademacher directions estimates input Tr(H^2); training deliberately reaches 100% accuracy so difficult or conflicting points are memorized and curvature is accumulated over time.
assumptions: High local input-loss curvature is specifically associated with sample memorization rather than generic fragility.
Input scaling, augmentation, architecture, and regularization permit meaningful relative ranks.
Intentional overfitting is computationally and ethically acceptable for the audit dataset.

techniques.role: Measures magnitude of positive and negative local loss curvature.
Avoids materializing the Hessian or second-order gradients.
Stabilizes scores against late margin-maximization collapse.

evaluations.setting: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10/100, and ImageNet with ResNet18
evaluations.metric: Visual semantics of top- and bottom-curvature samples
evaluations.result: High-ranked samples are often rare, ambiguous, mislabeled, multi-object, dark/low-contrast, or label-conflicting.

evaluations.metric: Cosine similarity with Feldman-Zhang memorization scores
evaluations.result: Overall similarity reaches 0.82/0.72 with weight decay and 0.90/0.87 on the highest-scored subsets.
evaluations.baseline: Influence-estimation scores from thousands of trained models

evaluations.result: Curvature beats inconfidence throughout and usually Confident Learning, with AUROC 84.3-100% across reported datasets/noise levels.

limitations: Computing random-direction gradient differences over many epochs is still more expensive than ordinary single-run training.
The score is tied to input coordinates, cross-entropy, intentional overfitting, architecture, and regularization; invariance across these choices is not established.
High curvature conflates annotation error with valid rare, ambiguous, or low-contrast examples and therefore cannot automate deletion.
failure_modes: Late softmax saturation lowers per-epoch curvature, so endpoint-only scoring misses memorized points.
Weight decay changes which conflicts appear and improves agreement with one comparator while hiding duplicates.
Auditors may remove valuable long-tail examples after interpreting high rank as proof of mislabeling.
reusable_insights: Dataset-audit scores should be triage signals paired with human review and complementary detectors.
Average training-dynamics measures across the phase where memorization occurs rather than reading only the endpoint.
Validate scalable proxies both against a causal expensive metric and controlled injected failures.
open_questions: How stable are curvature ranks across seeds, architectures, augmentations, and input parameterizations?
Can an online low-frequency estimator preserve audit quality at ImageNet or web scale?
Can decomposed scores distinguish valuable rare samples from corrupted or adversarial ones?

competitive_landscape.title: What Neural Networks Memorize and Why: Discovering the Long Tail via Influence Estimation
competitive_landscape.difference: Feldman-Zhang estimates a sample's causal influence using many retrainings; curvature is a one-model local proxy that also flags some conflicting duplicates.

competitive_landscape.title: Identifying Mislabeled Data using the Area Under the Margin Ranking
competitive_landscape.difference: AUM aggregates class-margin rankings and is cheap; curvature measures local input sensitivity and is motivated as memorization rather than only label-error detection.

competitive_landscape.title: Confident Learning: Estimating Uncertainty in Dataset Labels
competitive_landscape.difference: Confident Learning estimates joint noisy/true-label structure from out-of-sample probabilities; curvature intentionally overfits one model and ranks examples by second-order input-loss geometry.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: per-example memorization, training-dynamics audits, and Hessian estimators predate the work. The new combination is epoch-averaged input-loss Tr(H^2) as a one-model memorization proxy, with duplicate-conflict discovery and synthetic-noise validation.
reviewer_notes: Main text, dynamics, hyperparameter discussion, and image appendices were checked. Primary competitor records checked 2026-08-23. Curvature is useful triage evidence, not a ground-truth label-error oracle.
